title: Grundablauf: Erstellung, Gilde, Dungeon-Vertrag, Kampf, Abgabe
brief: Start a new campaign as a new player would. Create a Mage with the skills Flame Lance and Blink. Go into the city you start near, find the Adventurers' Guild, register as a member and read the board for your rank (Novice). Take a contract that sends you into a dungeon to fight, register it at the front desk, travel to that dungeon and go in onto its first level. Fight what the contract asks for until it is done, then go back to the Guild hall and turn the contract in.

milestones.goal: Create the character: the Base Class Mage, then the two skills Flame Lance and Blink.
Go into the city to the Adventurers' Guild and register as a member (pay what the Guild asks).
Read the Guild's board for your rank.
Take a contract from the board that sends you into a dungeon to fight (a cull, a clear or a hunt there) and register it at the front desk.
Travel to that dungeon and go in past its gate onto level 1.
Fight the dungeon's foes and win a fight. When you attack one of a group, watch how the others react.
Do what the contract asks until the contract slip shows it is done (READY).
If the level's guardian comes within reach and you feel strong enough, fight it.
If it comes within reach, clear the level.
Leave the dungeon, go back to the Guild hall and turn the contract in at the front desk.

focus: When you attack one enemy of a group in the open, do the others of the group react and join the fight, or do they stay where they were?
Do the numbers agree: how many foes the contract asks for on the board, on the contract slip in the HUD, and what the front desk says?
Do the HUD (HP, MP, enemies, the contract) and the narrator's story agree after each turn?
Does the story narrate things a System panel says did not happen (NOT TAKEN, REFUSED, BLOCKED)?
Note waits that feel too long and replies that cut off or come back empty.
personas: cautious: you look around before you act, ask before you commit, and keep an eye on your mana
direct: you go straight for each goal and attack early
talkative: you speak with the clerk and the people you meet and ask them questions before you act
tactical: you use both skills on purpose, pick your targets (the nearest, the wounded) and keep your distance
